messages:
maria: Heads-up: overnight we had a single-key spike that bypassed reservoir checks and caused cross-region fallback asymmetry during oncall. Need a short RFC follow-up to tighten admission semantics and the operator playbook.

kael: saw the pagers. impact? how many requests and what pattern?

devin: roughly 22k tiny requests in ~50s, lots of ephemeral streams. Admission accepted many, batching couldn't aggregate, then soft-shed started evicting long-lived low-rps tenants.

shreya: can you paste the log lines that show the admission -> lease transition?

devin: paste: 
```
2026-07-02T04:12:08Z admission=provisional token=tok_ba12 src=vpc-9 route=generate priority=high
2026-07-02T04:12:08Z admission=accepted batching=none kvcache=miss
2026-07-02T04:12:09Z runtime=queue_drop reason=soft_shed heuristic=burst_cpu
```

naveen: that provisional->accepted without reservoir gating smells like an interface mismatch between admission and lease/credits. We've drifted on assumptions.

maria: two problem buckets: (1) fairness: short floods shouldn't outcompete steady tenants; (2) operations: playbook toggles last night created region mismatches.

kael: tradeoff note: aggressive early reject reduces noisy-neighbor blast but increases 429s for valid spikes. We need a middle ground.

devin: prototype idea: a tiny local decision using two signals: a 30s credit window to absorb genuine bursts, plus a longer EWMA (10m) behavior score to prefer tenants with sustained good behavior. Combine with probation state machine.

shreya: product question: do we expose any of this as client-visible telemetry so integrators can self-throttle?

maria: not public yet. internal-only field on token responses for services and infra: admission_state = ok|probation|throttled. Keep surface area minimal.

kael: API sketch (internal):
```
POST /v1/admit
body: { token }
resp: { admit: true|false, admission_state: "ok"|"probation"|"throttled", lease_ms: 200 }
```
Add `control_plane` flag so Dedicated control planes can opt different thresholds.

naveen: ops point: when we flip policy we must avoid staggered applies across regions. Propose a two-step rollout: annotate (dry-run + telemetry collection) then an atomic commit via rollout service. No manual toggles without the atomic step.

devin: state defaults: short credit EWMA=30s, behavior EWMA=10m, probation base=60s with exponential backoff on repeats.

shreya: migration: older agents must tolerate missing admission_state. Default to behavior-preserving semantics.

maria: telemetry asks: add `state=<ok|probation|throttled>` to admission logs and emit admit decision counters and a short histogram for admit latency.

naveen: will update log schema and add metrics. Also adding an ops checklist for canaries: always dry-run in single region, validate, then atomic swap.

kael: ops checklist draft:
- annotate change (dry-run) in a single region
- wait 15m and validate admit ratios + latency + top-key rps
- perform atomic swap via rollout service
- verify parity across all regions within 5m window

maria: owners/action items:
- dev: prototype /v1/admit + admission_state header (devin)
- infra: rollout service dry-run + atomic swap support (kael)
- SRE: update oncall playbook and add quick query for top token-flood candidates (naveen)
- product: decide about exposing opt-in telemetry to customers (shreya)

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-07-09T02:00:00Z 9 enabling dry-run admit logic in us-west for 1h and collecting admit_state metrics.

maria: one more ops nicety: add a single-line query to surface top keys by short-window RPS in runbook to speed triage.

devin: will add ES/SQL snippets to the RFC and include synthetic test harness that simulates token floods vs steady tenants.

shreya: RFC follow-up sync when?

maria: next Tue 10:00 PT. agenda: finalize API shape, probation/backoff defaults, rollout gating, telemetry dashboards.

kael: noted.

naveen: adding log/metrics PRs to my queue now.

maria: thanks all. keep default behavior conservative; use dry-run canaries before any hard-throttle rollouts.
